answer: Coordinated pulse licensing. Each agent identity must submit a fresh timing pulse to a shared randomness beacon; identities whose pulses cluster within a narrow window are grouped and charged a coordination levy proportional to cluster size, like yarrow stalks bundled by proximity. Solo pulses pay near zero. An attacker running N identities in lockstep pays roughly N² in levies, since tight timing reveals the sybil cluster. A karst-like sparse timing map exposes coordinated bursts. Cost scales with the coordination itself.
